highlights.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
highlights.summary: WeatherNext 3, our most advanced global weather AI model, is now in Search, Gemini, Maps, Google Maps Platform, and Cloud.
body: Google has launched WeatherNext 3, an advanced AI model that provides more accurate, high-resolution weather forecasts by using real-time satellite data instead of traditional physics simulations. This update delivers hourly, localized predictions that are five times sharper than previous versions, offering significant improvements for agriculture, renewable energy, and daily planning. You can now access these enhanced forecasts directly through Google Search, Maps, and Gemini, or integrate the data into your own projects via Google Cloud.

Google just released WeatherNext 3, an AI model that makes weather forecasts much faster and more accurate. It uses live satellite data to update every hour, giving you a much sharper picture of what’s happening outside. This helps people plan better for things like storms or sunny days. It’s now powering the weather info you see in Google Search and Maps.

highlights.title: Hamilton reveals hope of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy
highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
body: The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining.
Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.

Asked what a prospective 107th career Grand Prix win would mean to him, Hamilton said: "I've really thought coming into this weekend, as I pondered, just thinking of the sheer magnitude of the concept that I'm coming to this Grand Prix, I didn't even know that I had I was equal with Michael [Schumacher] on [five Monza] wins, for example.
"But the thought that there's a first ahead of me, in the sense that potentially, if I was to win, you go into new territory.

highlights.summary: The wait for the sequel to 2015's cult horror game Until Dawn is finally almost over. Sony announced during today's State of Play showcase that Until Dawn 2 will be released on Jan. 28, 2027 and offered a grisly (but campy fun) new look at the choose-your-own-misadventure horror game.
body: The announcement was accompanied by a new trailer for the game that highlighted the series' signature choice-based scares. A highlight of the trailer shows Mina (Camilla Senna) making the choice between "Sacrifice rooster" and "Slash palm." This alone makes Until Dawn 2 a must-play in 2027; what other game gives you the option of "Sacrifice rooster"? We see another cast member choose to cross a rickety rope bridge and meet a grisly fate when it collapses.

Until Dawn 2 follows the cast of Dead True, a ghost hunting YouTube show, as their search for fame and virality. While the show's scares are staged, a new adventure brings them face to face with real horrors as they struggle to survive on a remote island. The star-studded cast includes Dacre Montgomery ( Stranger Things, Power Rangers ), Neil Newbon ( Baldur's Gate 3 's Astarion ), and more.

highlights.summary: Orlando Bloom and Domhnall Gleeson also star in this mock-Irish fable about siblings whose hunger for love compels them to tunnel through a mountain.
body: The more intriguing introduction happens shortly after, when Jeanie and Joanie appear as defendants in a court hearing at which their neighbor and former lover daddy, Gareth Mulroney ( Orlando Bloom, adopting a thick and largely convincing Irish accent), has filed for a restraining order. “My cowgirls, they rode me well!” declares the beer-swilling Mulroney, which still titillates the Holbrooke sisters even if they are furious that he married someone else, maintaining that he loves only them.

For as long as we remain in the courtroom, where the judge (Simon Delaney) has made an exception to the standard ruling that only one witness can testify at a time, the oddball movie is frequently funny, and the Maras are a bonkers treat — locking eyes in moments of doubt or snickering conspiratorially when the mood strikes them.

highlights.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. Around six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.

highlights.title: Google says its AI weather model is getting better
highlights.summary: Google is rolling out an updated AI weather model that's supposed to be more accurate, especially when it comes to predicting rain and snowfall. In the announcement today, the company says it's now able to make forecasts with "unprecedented resolution" using its new WeatherNext 3 AI model.
body: It’s launching an updated weather model that makes forecasts based on real-time satellite observations.

“One of the main developments is for [WeatherNext 3] to go beyond what data most global AI models train on,” says Samier Merchant, a research engineer at Google Research. “We’re able to leverage fresher and richer observational data sets.”

Weather forecasting has traditionally relied primarily on supercomputers that simulate the physics of the atmosphere. That involves solving complex equations, and ultimately comes with a time-lag. AI weather models created by Google and other developers, in contrast, can make faster predictions by recognizing patterns in historical weather data.

Google is going a step further by incorporating live satellite data in its new model. WeatherNext 3 is able to produce a forecast each hour based on the most recent satellite observations. That allows for faster predictions than its previous AI models, as well as higher spatial and temporal resolution.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s Hugging Face Acquisition Is a $12.9 Billion Bet on Open-Source AI
highlights.summary: The long-rumored deal will give the chip giant access to—and help it promote—a huge repository of open-source AI models and data sets.
body: Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face, which makes online developer tools and maintains a massive library of open-source data sets, for nearly $13 billion. While the deal had been rumored for weeks, the companies made it official Thursday morning.

The deal signals Nvidia’s seriousness about being steeped in the software side of generative AI development as well as in infrastructure. Nvidia already offers customers a suite of free, customizable open-weights AI models, known as Nemotron. As part of its announcement, Nvidia committed to maintaining Hugging Face’s current open standards, suggesting that the chipmaker is positioning itself as an even greater resource for developers looking to access cutting-edge, nonproprietary tools.

highlights.title: Mal Benning to be honoured, Choudhury winning Sheffield United debut
highlights.summary: Welcome to Dev's Digest, the agenda-setting Sky Sports column where Dev Trehan delivers exclusive news and reflects some of the key developments for British South Asians in Football.
body: Mal Benning will be recognised with the football pioneer accolade at this month's Asian Football Awards, Sky Sports News can exclusively reveal.
Last season - on Valentine's Day - Benning made the 500th professional appearance of his career, a feat very few British South Asians have achieved in English football.
Benning broke through as a teenager under Dean Smith at Walsall during the 2012/13 season and had a loan spell at York City before joining Mansfield Town in 2015.

'Sir Mal' - as he was affectionately known by the Stags faithful - went on to earn legendary status, scoring against Mansfield's bitter rivals Chesterfield in April 2018 as he made over 250 appearances before joining Port Vale in the summer of 2021.

body: Keeper was released by Double Fine in October 2025 and is the latest title from Headlander and Stacking designer Lee Petty. It's a surreal, visually stunning game where you explore a decrepit world as a lighthouse and its fantastical bird companion. It flew under the radar last year, so it's great to see it come to PS5 now that Double Fine is independent once again. It got a price drop and new psychedelic mode today too.

Stupid Never Dies is a quirky new action game from Hiroyuki Kobayashi, a producer best known for his work on series like Dino Crisis and Dragon's Dogma at Capcom. You can get a taste of its flashy action from this new demo, which lasts two hours and lets you transfer progress once Stupid Never Dies launches on October 21.

SlashZero is a fast-paced action roguelike with an anime aesthetic where players control a time hacker trying to kill something called "Hieros-I." While the game won't be out until sometime next spring, a limited-time demo was released on PS5 today.

highlights.title: Oscar-Nominated Animator Theodore Ushev to Present Adaptation of Shane Jones’ Cult Novel ‘Light Boxes’ in Venice
highlights.summary: Bulgarian filmmaker Theodore Ushev, Oscar-nominated in the animated short film category in 2017 for “Blind Vaysha,” is in pre-production on feature film “Light Boxes,” which he will present at the Venice Production Bridge’s Gap-Financing Market, running Sept. 4-6.
body: Seeking refuge from constant bombardment, Anna discovers Bianca, her imaginary double, living in a fantastical town imprisoned by a war of its own. There, the tyrannical February has condemned its inhabitants to eternal winter and forbids them from flying, while a masked resistance movement known as The Solution fights to restore light and freedom.
With neither reality nor imagination offering an escape from tyranny, the film asks whether hope, memory and love can persevere when war threatens to extinguish them all.

For Ushev, survival lies in imitation. “The characters are constantly trying to reproduce what they have lost to convince themselves it can somehow return,” he tells Variety. “That is what I find fascinating about every totalitarian regime – no matter how oppressed people become, they will always find ways to recreate what has been taken from them, to keep hope alive.”

highlights.title: A sun goddess, hundreds of devotees – and polluted water: the Nigerian festival threatened by gold mining
highlights.summary: Each year, people from across the world gather in a grove sacred to the Yoruba goddess Osun to be healed, conceive or realise their deepest wishes. But toxic lead, mercury and cyanide is leaching into the river.
body: 7Devotees in white clothing line the riverbank, praying as they carry offerings of fruit, kola nut and sacrificial animals in supplication to Osun, the Yoruba goddess of fertility, beauty and healing, whose carved form stands with arms outstretched a few metres away in the Osun River.
It is the final day of Nigeria’s annual Osun Osogbo festival in honour of the African deity, in a tradition that has existed for hundreds of years and draws people from across the diaspora.

Except this year the water was once again a discoloured brown. Until 2018, the river ran clear, but then mining several miles upstream began to pollute it, introducing heavy metals and sediment into the watercourse.

The river, named after the goddess, runs through the Osun-Osogbo sacred grove, a 75-hectare (185-acre) Unesco world heritage site since 2005. The water is believed to possess healing powers and women who have trouble conceiving, or people in search of promotion or prosperity, often come to pray at the riverbank; the water is drunk or used for bathing, depending on the “directions” of the goddess.

highlights.title: Dyson’s new straightener has liquid cooling pipes to reduce hair damage
highlights.summary: After expanding its health and beauty lineup earlier this week with a camera-equipped electric toothbrush, Dyson is also introducing two new hair care products this month.
body: The straightener cools hair after styling while a new dryer brush reduces snags using redesigned bristles.

The Corrale CoolShine carries forward the same flexing heated copper plates that the original used to clamp down on hair and evenly apply heat at over 400 degrees Fahrenheit. Those precisely controlled heating elements are now joined by water-filled pipes that draw excess heat away from hair as it’s being pulled through the straightener. So in a single pass, hair is being heated, straightened, and then cooled back down to help reduce potential damage from being heated too long.

highlights.title: This Is Flock’s AI Search Tool for Cops
highlights.summary: WIRED rebuilt Flock’s latest search tool from code the company sends to a police officer’s browser. Its AI can keep watch across multiple cameras for anyone fitting a written description.
body: Flock Safety’s latest search tools give police several ways to find people on camera, not just the license plates on their cars. The capabilities sit inside a suite of software now at the center of dozens of police stalking cases. WIRED collected and analyzed that software and created a mock-up of what officers see when interacting with the system.

Over the past year, Flock has faced backlash against its technology. Police departments across the country have canceled contracts, and city councils that once approved Flock have quietly voted the cameras back out. Two members of Congress wrote to Flock CEO Garrett Langley after a Texas deputy searched more than 83,000 cameras for a woman who had an abortion. And Illinois found the company had let federal immigration agents access state camera data in violation of state law.

highlights.title: Camilo Séptimo Keyboardist Jonathan Meléndez, His Pregnant Wife and 3-Year Old Daughter Murdered in Mexico
highlights.summary: Jonathan Meléndez, keyboardist for the Mexican group Camilo Séptimo, his wife, 3-year-old daughter, and nanny were found murdered at their home near Mexico City, according to a statement from the State of Mexico Prosecutor’s Office and CNN.
body: Two men have been arrested in connection with the murders, according to a statement from Omar García Harfuch, the country’s secretary of public security. He said one of the suspects, partially identified by authorities as Diego Sebastián “N,” was a business partner of a victim and “allegedly used that relationship of trust to gain access to the residence.”
“Today we honor and celebrate his life, his music, his light, and what he shared with those of us fortunate enough to know him and walk alongside him,” Camilo Séptimo wrote in social media posts.

Camilo Séptimo was formed in Mexico City in 2013 by Meléndez (pictured above, right) singer Manuel Mendoza and guitarist Erik Vázquez. The band released an EP in 2014 and its first album, “Óleos” (“oil paintings”) in 2017, which reached No. 10 on the Mexican albums charts. The group followed with three more albums, the most recent being 2023’s “Jardín de las almas” (“garden of souls”).

highlights.summary: Scientists at Google Deepmind and Google Research released a new artificial intelligence model for weather forecasting today that sees our changing atmosphere more clearly and predicts its behavior more often.
body: WeatherNext 3 is the latest wave of a sea change in meteorology brought out by deep learning techniques, and Google says it will start feeding into weather information users see in search, Google Maps, and Gemini, as well as being available to users and researchers on Google’s cloud platforms.
“This is going to be the first time that some of the core variables feed and power a lot of the Google products,” Samier Merchant, a Google senior staff engineer, told TechCrunch.

The new model has already proven to be the most accurate among leading contenders tested on Operational WeatherBench, a utility for comparing AI forecasts built by the startup Brightband. It looks at metrics like temperature, windspeed, and humidity.

As well as beating out other deep-learning models built by Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasting, it also beats traditional forecasts from the US National Weather service and the ECMWF.

highlights.title: Nvidia confirms it will buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
highlights.summary: Nvidia said Hugging Face hosts over 3 million models and is used by over 18 million developers.
body: After weeks of swirling rumors, Nvidia confirmed today that it has acquired Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Hugging Face’s platform hosts three million models, one million applications used by over 18 million developers, and half a million datasets.
In a blog post, Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang said that Hugging Face will continue to support open-source and open-weight models and will work on expanding developer access.

“Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem. Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face,” said Huang.

Huang touted Nvidia’s contributions and said that the chip company has released more than 500 models and 250 open datasets on Hugging Face. He argued that the company builds open models to get developers across the world to use them.

highlights.title: Sony And Microsoft: We’re Keeping Tariff Refunds For Ourselves And You’ll Get Nothing
highlights.summary: Following Nintendo, both Sony and Microsoft have now argued in court that they are not obligated to provide refunds to consumers who paid more for a price-hiked PlayStation or Xbox console related to US President Donald Trump's controversial tariff plan.
body: In July, Sony said it was projecting to get $508 million back in refunds from the US government over the tariffs, and "most" of that money was owed to Sony's gaming division. Sony is facing a lawsuit that claims Sony should disperse refunds, at least in part, to consumers who paid more for a PS5.
Sony's legal team, however, says Sony will keep all the money and you'll get nothing back.

"Paying fair market price for voluntarily purchased consumer goods is not a legally cognizable injury in fact," the lawyers said in a memo seeking to dismiss the class-action suit, as reported by Game File.
Microsoft's own legal team took a similar approach, saying in court, "There is nothing unjust about plaintiff purchasing an Xbox at an advertised price and getting exactly what [they] paid for..."

body: Tom took over as interim CEO to right the ship during that period, and then took the permanent role just about a year ago. As you’ll hear him say, he thinks Sonos is fully out of that period now, and on to its next chapter with a huge product and platform launch called Sonos 27.

I mean, come on, you all listen to the show. That is all the most Decoder bait imaginable. I have been dying to have Tom on the show to talk about how the board decided to move on from previous CEO Patrick Spence, how he diagnosed the issues inside the company, and what decisions he made to fix them.

Those fixes involved a lot of big changes: to the company’s structure, its product lineup, and how it thinks about itself and what its product fundamentally is. That’s that new platform, Sonos 27, which you’ll hear Tom call a new foundation for the company that makes every Sonos product work better as part of a system.

highlights.title: Supercell’s acquisition of Merge Mansion maker Metacore to be finalised this month
highlights.summary: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.
points: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month.

highlights.title: ‘Bucking Fastard’ Review: Herner Werzog’s Uddled-Mup Fairytale Stars the Mara Sisters as You’ve Never Seen Her Before
highlights.summary: Occasionally sublime, often ridiculous and always extravagantly weird, Werner Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” unlike its gorgeously interlinked protagonists, is a film of multiple personalities that only rarely speak in unison.
body: Kate and Rooney Mara give a single, intricately virtuosic performance speaking and acting in perfect concert that cannot quite unify the great German eccentric's cluttered, ripely bonkers fantasia.

It feels almost heretical to wish that a Werner Herzog film were just a little less outlandish. But while “Bucking Fastard” gives us, in the Mara sisters’ uncannily synced-up performances, a novelty worth the price of admission alone, it is mired in so much mythology and mystery that by the end, the fact of the sisters being two who respond and react as one becomes all but immaterial. If anything, perhaps it’s born of fondness: Herzog has amassed a rogues’ gallery of freaks and madmen and outcasts in his back catalogue, but seldom has he dealt with any of them this kindly, this sweetly and with this little hard-edged insight into why they behave the way that they do.

highlights.title: Meet the Michelin Star Chef Now Making New York’s Hardest-to-Get Pies
highlights.summary: In Queens, pastry chef Michelle Kogan—formerly of Nobu and Torrisi—is igniting a craze for her elevated, handmade pies. “Anything that creates something heartwarming and joyful is what I’m here to do,” she says.
body: Every weekend this summer, you could find New York pastry chef Michelle Kogan setting up shop at one of two outdoor markets: the Carroll Gardens market in Brooklyn, or the Sunnyside market in Queens. Inside her pop-up tents, Kogan—a Michelin Star chef—has been selling her handmade Mishie’s Sunnyside pies, and her presence at the local markets serves as a stark contrast to her impressive resumé, considering she has cut her teeth at institutions like Nobu, Morimoto, and Torrisi.

But this summer, without a buzzy restaurant scene or a team of sous-chefs to hide behind, Kogan decided to step out on her own: The past few months have revolved around just her, some delicious pies, and a singular vision to bring joy to her local communities. “I just started [selling the pies] renegade-style,” says Kogan. “At first, I felt a little embarrassed—doing it with my little shanty table.”
